payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: pass: The mug is visibly to the right of the headphones. fail: The mug is visibly not to the right of the headphones. unknown: Their relative positions cannot be determined from the image.
node.binding: Inspect the edited image and compare the mug’s position with the headphones; this directly tests the requested outcome.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, the mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.

fulfillment: The node overweights the final-state relation and treats any positional change as progress. In the source, the mug is already left of the headphones; in the edit, the rightmost mug is right of them, but the image also shows an additional mug and a blurred mug-shaped remnant at the original location. Do not infer completion from “a mug” being right of the headphones: bind the same source mug across images and assess whether that object was moved, while accounting for duplication/remnant and uncertainty. The trace’s two pass observations do not establish that the requested object was moved or that the edit is complete; distinguish evidence of progress from evidence of fulfillment under the rubric, and lower confidence or return unknown if identity/change cannot be resolved. This is a semantic evidence/criterion issue, not a transport or schema failure.
s2: The binding is too vague to distinguish the requested mug from newly rendered copies. Make the check explicitly track the source mug across the before/after images using its appearance and original location, and assess whether that same object moved relative to the headphones; do not count a mug merely appearing on the right as progress. In this edit, the right-side mug coexists with a mug-shaped blur at the source location and another mug near the headphones, so duplication/remnant makes object identity and actual movement uncertain. Keep progress distinct from completion, and use unknown or reduced confidence when the same mug’s movement cannot be established rather than treating the final relation as decisive. This is a visual binding/criterion issue, not a transport or schema failure.

response.content: {"text":"The check only tests whether some mug is right of the headphones, so it mistakes a final-state relation for evidence that the requested mug was moved and completed. Bind the mug in the source image (the blue mug left of the headphones) to its counterpart in the edit, and assess change across both images rather than counting any right-side mug. The edit shows a blurred remnant at the source location and multiple differently rendered mugs, so identity and movement are ambiguous; do not assert fulfillment from the rightmost mug alone. Keep progress distinct from completion and use uncertainty/reduced confidence when the same mug’s movement cannot be established. This is a visual binding and criterion issue, not a transport or schema failure."}
